what_happened: While handling job 20261028-065911-m6m5 (the replay job), the operator told the scope guard and Sri that retrying it would resume the kept candidate and cost only a verifier call, about $0.50. The retry instead re-planned and rebuilt from scratch. It cost $4.92 and stopped on low disk at the same point as before. The operator had assumed that keep-and-resume covers environment stops, but it covers only timeouts, and did not check before quoting the cost. No work was judged bad. The money was spent on a retry that could not get past the disk limit.
cause: Athena does not tell the person retrying a job what the retry will do. The choice between resuming a kept candidate and re-planning from scratch depends on why the job stopped. Only timeouts keep a candidate. That rule is hidden in code, and nothing states the mode or a cost estimate before the retry spends money. The person deciding must guess from memory, and the guess goes unchecked. A retry of a job that stopped on low disk also re-runs into the same resource limit, because no check says the cause is still present.
prevention: Make retry state its plan before spending anything. Retry should print whether it will resume the kept candidate or re-plan and rebuild, why (the stop reason), and an estimated cost range from past attempts. Where the stop was an environment reason such as low disk, retry should keep the candidate as it does for timeouts, and refuse or warn if the cause (free disk) is still present. Anyone quoting a retry cost then reads it from this output instead of assuming.
proposed_request: Change `athena retry` so it states its plan and cost before running, and so environment stops resume like timeouts. Outcomes: (1) Before any paid stage runs, `athena retry <job>` prints the stop reason of the earlier attempt, whether it will resume the kept candidate or re-plan and rebuild, and an estimated cost range taken from the cost of earlier stages of that job. A `--dry-run` flag prints this and exits without spending anything. (2) When an attempt stopped for an environment reason (low free disk), Athena keeps the candidate as it does for a timeout, so retry resumes at the verifier and checks instead of re-planning. (3) If the environment cause is still present when retry starts (free disk is still under the guard threshold), retry refuses with a message naming the shortfall, and does not spend money. (4) The scope guard does not count the cost of an environment-stopped attempt as progress-less spend on the line. Acceptance: tests show that a job stopped on a timeout and a job stopped on low disk are each retried in resume mode and print the mode and estimate; a test shows that retry with disk still low refuses without calling any paid stage; a test shows --dry-run makes no paid call. Use the existing guard and record validation rules. Keep the change within the retry command, the keep-candidate logic and their tests.
